points.description: States abstraction as an advantage of OOP (hiding complex implementation details and exposing only essentials).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only vaguely related (e.g. encapsulation/data hiding/simplicity) without naming abstraction.

points.description: States reusability as an advantage of OOP (code can be reused, e.g. through classes and inheritance).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the idea is vaguely stated (e.g. 'less code to write' or 'easy maintenance') without reuse.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both advantages: abstraction and reusability, in any wording. Give part marks for a vague or related idea such as encapsulation or easier maintenance. Wrong claims lose only their own point; extra correct advantages are fine but earn nothing extra.
